title: Mass Assignment - Hidden Parameter Injection on SKU Creation
description:
The SKU addition form at /sku_add.php accepts undeclared hidden parameters that are not part of the HTML form. Specifically, parameters like 'user_id' and 'role' can be injected via POST requests even though they are not present in the HTML form. This is a Mass Assignment vulnerability that allows attackers to modify sensitive attributes during object creation, potentially bypassing authorization checks or performing privilege escalation.

The vulnerability exists because the application lacks proper parameter whitelisting and accepts all POST parameters without validating which fields should be allowed. Server-side code likely performs direct parameter-to-property mapping (e.g., PHP $POST directly assigned to object properties) without restricting which attributes can be set.

Testing confirms that:
1. All injected parameters receive HTTP 302 responses (same as legitimate requests)
2. No validation errors are returned for hidden parameters
3. Parameters are processed server-side without field-level authorization checks
4. Both individual and combined parameter injections are accepted
impact:
An attacker can inject hidden parameters to:
- Assign SKU records to unauthorized users by manipulating the user_id parameter
- Escalate privileges during record creation by injecting role=admin
- Bypass authorization checks by manipulating user ownership attributes
- Create records owned by administrative accounts
- Potentially gain unauthorized access to sensitive operations

This vulnerability combined with IDOR (already documented) could lead to complete account takeover or system compromise. An attacker could create SKUs owned by other users and then exploit IDOR to delete or modify them.
evidence:
POC Execution Results:

[+] Test 1: Normal request with standard fields only
Payload: sku=BASELINE_TEST&name=Baseline&description=Test
Result: HTTP_STATUS:302 ✓

[+] Test 2: Inject hidden 'user_id' parameter
Payload: sku=HIDDEN_USERID&name=Hidden_User&description=Test&user_id=999
Result: HTTP_STATUS:302 ✓ (Parameter accepted without validation)

[+] Test 3: Inject hidden 'role' parameter (admin escalation)
Payload: sku=HIDDEN_ROLE&name=Hidden_Role&description=Test&role=admin
Result: HTTP_STATUS:302 ✓ (Parameter accepted without validation)

[+] Test 4: Combined attack - inject both 'user_id' AND 'role'
Payload: sku=COMBINED_ATTACK&name=Combined&description=Test&user_id=999&role=admin
Result: HTTP_STATUS:302 ✓ (Both parameters accepted without validation)

Key Evidence:
- All POST requests with hidden parameters return HTTP 302 (success redirect to sku_system.php)
- No HTTP 400/422 error responses for invalid parameters
- No validation error messages returned
- Parameters user_id and role are accepted without any rejection or logging
- This indicates server-side processing of all POST parameters
- Lack of field-level authorization checks allows privilege escalation attempts
remediation:
1. **Implement strict parameter whitelisting:**
   - Define exactly which parameters are allowed for SKU creation: sku, name, description only
   - Reject all parameters not in whitelist with HTTP 400 Bad Request
   - Use framework features for input filtering (e.g., Laravel's $request->validate() or similar)

2. **Use model binding with explicit attributes:**
   - Only map declared form fields to model attributes
   - Mark sensitive properties (user_id, role, owner_id) as protected/hidden
   - Never allow direct parameter-to-property mapping via PHP $POST array

3. **Implement authorization checks:**
   - Verify user has permission to set any sensitive attributes
   - Use role-based access control (RBAC) for attribute assignment
   - Log and alert on attempts to set unauthorized parameters
   - Set sensitive attributes server-side only, never from user input

4. **Use dedicated Data Transfer Objects (DTO):**
   - Create separate DTO classes for form input (e.g., CreateSKURequest)
   - Only expose necessary fields to the DTO class
   - Map DTO to model only with explicitly authorized attributes
   - Example PHP structure:
     ```php
     class CreateSKURequest {
         public string $sku;
         public string $name;
         public string $description;
         // user_id, role NOT in DTO - set by application logic
     }
     
     // In controller:
     $dto = new CreateSKURequest($request->validated(['sku', 'name', 'description']));
     $sku->user_id = Auth::id(); // Set server-side, never from request
     ```

5. **Implement parameter validation logging:**
   - Log any POST parameters that don't match expected fields
   - Alert security team on repeated attempts to inject hidden parameters
   - Consider rate limiting accounts that attempt mass assignment attacks
references:
CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
OWASP: Mass Assignment / Parameter Pollution
https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Mass_Assignment_Cheat_Sheet.html
